title: Open-world people 2: wanderers, hunters and the dead
prompt: A line-up of blocky voxel characters at the same scale, each front-on and from the high three-quarter game angle: Coach Gleeson Hedge, a short, loud satyr in a red tracksuit and a baseball cap with a whistle and a wooden club; Zoë Nightshade, lieutenant of the Hunters of Artemis, dark braided hair, silver circlet and parka, a silver bow; Rachel Elizabeth Dare, a mortal girl with frizzy red hair in paint-splattered jeans with a sketchbook; Quintus, a grizzled swordsman with grey hair and a fencing sword (secretly the inventor Daedalus, with a faint bronze glint at the neck); Phoebe and Bianca di Angelo, Hunters of Artemis in silver parkas; Charon, the ferryman of the dead, in a sharp Italian suit and sunglasses with a boat pole; and Sisyphus, a weary old Greek in a ragged tunic leaning on his boulder. 3D game art in the blocky voxel style of Minecraft Dungeons: characters built from cubes, with a large cube head whose face is simple pixel art (about 8 × 8 pixels: pixel eyes, a pixel mouth, hair drawn as pixels and as a few blocky tufts), a boxy torso, square arms and legs, crisp pixel-art textures (about 16 pixels per block) with simple shading, chunky readable silhouettes; warm cinematic lighting, soft ambient occlusion and glowing magic effects. Costume colours and details follow the Camp Half-Blood cartoon concept art. Palette: camp orange #f28c28, sea teal #0f6f73, deep navy #10233d, jade #2e8b6e, coral #e8664a, bronze gold #c9963a, lightning yellow #ffd84a, parchment cream #f4ead5, vase black #17130f and owl grey #8c96a3. Flat light-grey background, no cast shadow. No lettering, logos, captions or watermark.
